frameworks.name: Founder Handoff Readiness
frameworks.definition: A decision framework for determining when a founder should exit day-to-day operations based on profit available to absorb management salary and founder's alternative ROI on freed time.

claims.text: A manager hire at $100,000 annual salary (versus $60-80k mid-market German labor cost) is justified when freed-up founder time can generate more than $100,000 in additional profit within the same period; if the founder cannot deploy their freed time to $400,000 in additional profit (to recover the salary and break even), the hire is premature.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Founder has quantified profit target ($450k baseline)
Founder has identified high-ROI use of freed time (marketing, business development)
Business margin covers management salary ($100k out of $450k profit = 22% reduction)
claims.mechanism: Founder time is capital; manager salary is only justified if the ROI on freed time exceeds the salary cost. A €100k hire that frees the founder to generate €400k incremental profit breaks even at 4:1 return.

numbers.axis: Manager salary to incremental profit multiple

bounded_by: Does not apply to businesses where founder's freed time has no alternative use
Does not apply when current business profit is insufficient to absorb salary (e.g., <€150k profit)

claims.text: Paying 20-30% premium for A-player talent over B-talent is the single largest ROI arbitrage still available in business, because A-players deliver 3-4x the output of B-players. Most founders avoid this spending due to fear of the extra cost, but the math shows the premium is cheaper than hiring 3-4 lower-tier replacements.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Role is outcome-critical (operations manager, sales lead, etc.)
Business has cash flow to absorb the 20-30% premium
Founder can accurately identify A-talent from B-talent
claims.mechanism: Talent quality is a leverage multiplier. One A-player at €100k produces 3-4x output of a B-player at €75k. Hiring three B-players (€225k total) to match one A-player's output is more expensive and creates coordination overhead; A-player is the capital-efficient choice.

numbers.axis: Talent tier vs. output multiplier and total cost

anchors.region: Multiple B-players needed to match A-player output

bounded_by: Does not apply to low-skill roles where output is commoditized (entry-level labor)
Does not apply when the business cannot retain A-talent (culture/compensation ceiling)

claims.text: For a €1.8M revenue e-commerce business running at 25% gross margin and €450k profit, the critical decision point for hiring a manager is whether the founder's freed time can be deployed to €400k in incremental profit (to break even on a €100k manager salary and create positive ROI).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Business model is distribution/resale (low margin, capital-light ops)
Founder is currently working in fulfillment/operations
Freed time target is marketing and business development (higher-margin opportunities)

numbers.axis: E-commerce revenue to profit ratio and founder time value

anchors.region: Manager salary as % of profit (€100k manager)
Incremental profit required to break even on hire

bounded_by: Assumes margin stays constant at 25% (may erode if volume scales without unit-economics improvement)
Assumes freed founder time is actually deployed to profitable activities (not diffused into low-ROI work)

examples.text: A German e-commerce founder running a Shopify store selling branded bike parts via Google Shopping ads reached €1.8M annual revenue with €450k profit at 25% margins. Caught in daily operations (customer support, warehouse work), the founder aimed to scale to €5M in two years. When asked whether to hire a manager at €100k/year to free time for marketing and business development, Alex Hormozi worked through the math: €100k salary removes €100k from profit (down to €350k net), so the freed time must generate €400k in incremental profit to break even. The founder confirmed they could achieve this through expanded marketing channels and product sourcing, making the hire immediately justified.

practices.text: When evaluating a management hire, always calculate the breakeven incremental profit required (manager salary × opportunity-cost multiple of 4:1 for strong ROI) and verify the founder's ability to deploy freed time to that level of output before committing.
Favor A-talent hires even at 20-30% salary premium over B-talent hires, because the output multiplier (3-4x) makes the higher cost a capital-efficient investment.
